evidence: prerequisites.py:226-229 `# Per-call: the ladder may have escalated `model`, so resolve the model-max output budget AFTER the model swap` then `call_cfg = passes._max_output_cfg(dataclasses.replace(cfg, model=model))`
prerequisites.py:260-265 escalation path `ladder = sizing.models_at_or_above(model)` ... `return run_bin(bin_, next_model, attempt + 1)`
_Recorder.run (test file lines ~40) always returns a canned dict and never raises, so run_bin never hits `is_context_limit_error` / ladder escalation
test asserts only `all(mt == _SONNET_MAX ...)` on the single un-escalated call
advisory.finding: The prerequisite run_bin's specific new contract — resolve the model-max output budget AFTER a ladder model escalation (so the raised model's HIGHER cap is used) — is untested. test_prerequisite_finder_carries_model_max_output drives run_focused_finder through a _Recorder that never raises a context-limit error, so run_bin's escalation branch (recurse to next_model on the ladder) never executes; the widen is only exercised on the initial, un-escalated model. A regression that computed model-max from the pre-swap (lower) model would not be caught.
scenarios: A refactor moves _max_output_cfg before the model swap, or reads cfg.model instead of the escalated model, silently re-capping an escalated call at the smaller model's max
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a fake runner whose first call raises a context-limit error and whose second (escalated) call records its request.config.max_tokens; assert the escalated call's cap equals the escalated model's model_max_output_tokens.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Exclude `summarize_for_isf` from the model-max output raise (or give it its own bounded output cap) so the ISF summary stays small enough to fit the window it is compressing for.
evidence: passes.py:540-545 docstring: 'Compress an oversized session log to fit the ISF context window ... Used only when the log exceeds the budget'

pass1.py:387-397: summary is only produced when `est_tokens(text) > budget` (window headroom − P8_OUTPUT_RESERVE_TOKENS) and the returned `summary` is fed back as the ISF `text`, so an oversized summary re-enters the same window-fit path

ABSENCE: the operator rule 'output bounded by the model's actual findings' does not hold for a summarizer whose job is to REDUCE size — no per-call bound keeps the summary compact once the 16000 hard cap is removed
dropped.finding: Blanket-applying `_max_output_cfg` to `summarize_for_isf` raises the ISF-summary output ceiling from 16000 to the model max (128000), but this call exists specifically to COMPRESS an oversized session log so it FITS the ISF context-window budget; an unbounded output cap lets the 'summary' grow large enough to re-exceed the very window budget the summarization was invoked to satisfy.
scenarios: An oversized ISF session log is summarized; the model produces a verbose 40K+ token summary that then overflows the ISF finder's window budget, re-raising the context-limit error the summarization step was meant to prevent
dropped.suggested_fix: Keep `summarize_for_isf` on the prior (bounded) `cfg` rather than `_max_output_cfg(cfg)`, or set an explicit `output_token_limit` sized to the ISF window budget so the summary cannot exceed the target it must fit.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Warn or raise on an unrecognized non-empty `output_budget` value instead of silently ignoring it.
evidence: ABSENCE: no else-branch or validation for an unrecognized non-empty `output_budget` value; a typo silently no-ops
dropped.finding: `runs.py` only acts on the exact literal `output_budget == 'model_max'`; any other value (e.g. a YAML typo like `model-max` or a future numeric budget) is silently ignored with no validation or warning, so a misconfigured step reverts to the default cap without any signal.
scenarios: An operator or future edit sets `output_budget: model-max` (hyphen) in a gate YAML; the step silently runs at DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS and truncates, exactly the failure mode this change remediates, with no diagnostic
